pharm: Standardized gum-resin extract of Boswellia serrata (frankincense) containing boswellic acids (notably AKBA) that inhibit 5-lipoxygenase, used as an anti-inflammatory supplement for osteoarthritis and other inflammatory conditions.
quick: Standardized extract ~250-300 mg daily (e.g., 30% AKBA); resin 300-400 mg 3x/day
Take with food to improve tolerance/absorption
summary: Boswellia serrata is a standardized gum-resin extract (frankincense) used as an herbal anti-inflammatory, most studied in knee osteoarthritis, and also explored in inflammatory bowel disease and asthma. Its active boswellic acids, especially AKBA (3-O-acetyl-11-keto-beta-boswellic acid), inhibit 5-lipoxygenase, reducing leukotriene synthesis. It is a dietary supplement and is not FDA-approved as a drug; it is not recommended by major osteoarthritis guidelines despite supportive trial data.
indications: Symptomatic relief of osteoarthritis (especially knee) pain and stiffness (traditional/supplement use)
Adjunct in chronic inflammatory conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease (investigational/traditional)

dosage.n: Pain reduction reported as early as ~7 days in trials
Common supplement regimen; standardization varies by product
Evidence limited; not a substitute for proven therapy

admin: Take orally with food to improve gastrointestinal tolerance and absorption
Use a product standardized for boswellic acid (and ideally AKBA) content, as potency varies widely between products
Allow several weeks for assessment of symptomatic benefit
Do not use as a replacement for guideline-recommended osteoarthritis or disease-specific therapy
Discontinue if significant GI upset or allergic reaction occurs
moa: Boswellic acids, particularly AKBA, act as specific non-redox inhibitors of 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX), reducing synthesis of pro-inflammatory leukotrienes (e.g., leukotriene B4); additional effects include suppression of inflammatory enzymes and mediators, contributing to reduced joint pain and protection against cartilage degradation in osteoarthritis models.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to Boswellia species or product components
relative: Active peptic ulcer or significant GI disease
Concurrent use with multiple anti-inflammatory or immune-modulating agents (limited data)

preg: Avoid during pregnancy; safety has not been established and some traditional sources suggest uterine stimulant potential.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding; insufficient safety data on excretion in milk or infant effects.
renal: No established dose adjustment; limited pharmacokinetic data. Use cautiously in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution; limited data. Discontinue if signs of liver injury develop.

moderate: Possible additive effect/altered handling with NSAIDs and other anti-inflammatory agents (theoretical)
May modulate CYP enzymes in vitro - caution with drugs of narrow therapeutic index (limited human data)
minor: May enhance effects of other immune-modulating supplements
interactions.food: Take with food to improve tolerance and absorption

rare: Reported hepatic enzyme elevation (rare, supplement context)

monitoring: Joint pain, stiffness, and functional response over several weeks
counsel: This is an herbal dietary supplement, not an FDA-approved medicine; quality and potency vary between brands
Take with food and allow a few weeks to judge benefit for joint symptoms
Do not stop your prescribed arthritis or other medicines without speaking to your clinician
Tell your clinician you are taking it, especially before surgery or if you take other medicines
pk: Symptomatic benefit over days to weeks; pain reduction reported by ~7 days in trials
Boswellic acids absorbed orally; improved with food/fat
Variable by acid (KBA/AKBA roughly several hours); not standardized
Store in a cool, dry place away from light per product label
pearls: NOTE: Dietary supplement, not FDA-approved as a drug; information drawn from clinical trial and traditional-use literature
Active anti-inflammatory mechanism is 5-LOX inhibition by boswellic acids (especially AKBA)
Product standardization matters greatly - look for stated boswellic acid and AKBA content
Not recommended by 2019 ACR/Arthritis Foundation osteoarthritis guidelines despite some positive trial data
Generally well tolerated; main adverse effects are mild GI symptoms
missed: If using on a fixed schedule, take the missed dose when remembered unless it is near the next dose; do not double. Consistent daily use over weeks is more important than a single dose.
overdose: Overdose data are limited; excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal upset. Manage supportively and discontinue use.
